Monitoring Response and Additional Therapy 

ISM or SSM 

Biopsy of involved extramedullary organ may be considered to evaluate 
the grade and extent of SM-related organ damage.109 Evaluation of organ 
damage in SM with an AHN might require a tissue biopsy to ascertain the 
relationship between organ damage and burden of mast cell infiltration 
and/or AHN involvement.109 Additional staging studies include CBC for the 
evaluation of hematologic organ damage, liver functions tests 
(measurement of total bilirubin, alanine aminotransferase, aspartate 
aminotransferase, and serum ALP [the most common SM-associated sign 
of hepatic damage]) for the evaluation of nonhematologic organ damage, 
and imaging studies (CT or MRI) to verify physical examination findings of 
organ involvement or organ damage. 

History and physical examination, laboratory evaluation (annually for 
patients with ISM and every 6 to 12 months for patients with SSM), 
baseline DEXA scan (with serial evaluation based on severity and extent 
of bony disease), and assessment of symptom burden and QOL using 
MSAF and MQLQ is recommended for patients with ISM and SSM. 

KIT D816V allele burden has been shown to correlate with serum tryptase 
levels and response to cytoreductive therapy. While incorporated into 
current clinical trials of KIT inhibitors, the role of KIT D816V allele burden 
monitoring during treatment has not been formally established in clinical 
practice.212,213 

Although increased serum beta-2-microglobulin has been identified in one 
study as an independent predictor of disease progression in patients with 
ISM, this is not routinely performed in clinical practice.17 Progressively 
increasing serum tryptase levels have been associated with disease 
progression to SSM or ASM and shorter PFS in patients with ISM.211

The Panel acknowledges that response criteria were developed mainly for 
use in clinical trials and that clinical benefit may not reach the threshold of 
these response criteria.109-111 Response assessment should be based on 
the improvement of symptoms related to mast cell mediator release and 
SM-related organ damage at the discretion of the clinician. 

surgery due to delayed mast cell mediator release.214 The primary goal is 
to prevent mast cell activation during and in the immediate aftermath of 
the surgical procedure. Multidisciplinary management is recommended 
with the involvement of surgical, anesthesia, and perioperative medical 
teams. Careful review of prior anesthetic records as well as identification 
and avoidance of known triggers for symptoms related to mast cell 
mediator release (such as temperature extremes [hypothermia or 
hyperthermia] and unnecessary trauma) are strongly recommended.215 

Continuation of prior treatment is recommended for patients achieving 
adequate response to anti-mediator drug therapy (symptomatic ISM or 
SSM) or cytoreductive therapy (advanced SM). Evaluation of allogeneic 
HCT should be considered an option for patients with advanced SM (ASM, 
SM-AHN when the SM component requires prioritization over the AHN 
component, or MCL with or without an AHN) with suitable performance 
status and if with adequate response to cytoreductive therapy and with 
suitable donor(s) are identified.206,209 

The efficacy and safety of perioperative drugs in patients with SM has not 
been fully established, although anecdotal reports suggest that certain 
perioperative drugs are considered safer in patients with SM.216 
Nevertheless, the use of perioperative drugs is not contraindicated in 
patients with SM.215,217 While it is important that analgesics should not be 
withheld from patients with SM (since pain can be a trigger for mast cell 
activation), caution should be exercised with the use of opioids (eg, 
codeine or morphine). 

For patients with ISM or SSM, a clinical trial is preferred if there is an 
inadequate response, intolerance, no response, or loss of response to 
initial treatment. Cladribine, peginterferon alfa-2a with or without 
prednisone, and midostaurin are treatment options that are useful in 
certain circumstances. Re-staging (as described above) is recommended 
for patients with symptomatic ISM or SSM with disease progression to 
advanced SM or for those with advanced SM with inadequate response, 
intolerance, no response, or loss of response. Subsequent-line therapy 
and allogeneic HCT should be considered for advanced SM. Clinical trials 
are always recommended for these orphan diseases, regardless of 
whether patients have ISM, SSM, or advanced forms of SM. 

Special Considerations 

Surgery 

Management of symptoms related to mast cell mediator release depends 
on their severity. The use of benzodiazepines, antihistamines (H1 and H2 
blockers), and corticosteroids is probably helpful in reducing the frequency 
and/or severity of symptoms related to mast cell mediator release.215,216 
Other options include fluid resuscitation, intravenous epinephrine, and 
discontinuation of the suspected drug or anesthetic agent.215 The risk of 
anaphylaxis in the perioperative period is estimated to be higher in 
patients with SM relative to the general population.217 In the event of 
anaphylaxis or other mast cell activation event, a full allergic workup 
should be initiated.217,218 The workup should include skin tests or detection 
of specific IgE antibodies for the identification of IgE-mediated 
hypersensitivity to drugs and measurement of serum tryptase level within 
30 to 120 minutes of symptom onset and also after full recovery.215,216

potential risks during both pregnancy and lactation are summarized in the 
algorithm. 

COVID-19 Vaccination 

Although mast cells have been associated with beneficial effects in early 
stages of pregnancy (in terms of implantation, placentation, and fetal 
growth), in later stages of pregnancy, excessive release of mast cell 
mediators is associated with pre-term delivery.219 The diagnosis of SM 
does not appear to have any effect on fertility. There is limited evidence 
regarding the impact of mastocytosis on pregnancy compared to the 
general population. Spontaneous miscarriages and worsening of 
symptoms related to mast cell activation have been reported in 20% to 
30% of pregnant females with mastocytosis.220-222 Symptoms related to 
mast cell mediator release have been observed in 11% of patients without 
any fatal outcome.222 

Patients with mast cell leukemia are a unique population with the potential 
for mast cell activation and/or anaphylaxis with the COVID-19 vaccines. 
Recommendations from the ECNM and the American Initiative in Mast 
Cell Diseases were published and some general recommendations are 
listed below.227 Patients deemed at high risk for vaccination include those 
who have previously experienced grade 1 or 2 anaphylaxis, per Brighton 
consensus, after the first COVID-19 shot; those with known or suspected 
allergy to polyethylene glycol (PEG) or polysorbate 80/20; those with prior 
anaphylaxis following vaccination; and those with unstable mastocytosis 
and severe MCAS symptoms that are not controlled. Such patients should 
have two epinephrine autoinjectors with them and should receive the 
vaccine at a location with emergency awareness and that has equipment 
and drugs for resuscitation available. These individuals may also be 
evaluated by skin testing for vaccine components, such as PEG or 
polysorbate 80/20. Additionally, H1 antihistamine premedication should be 
used in these patients 1 hour before receiving the vaccine. Following 
vaccination, patients should also be supervised for 60 minutes. 

SM is not a contraindication to a successful pregnancy. Patients with SM 
who are pregnant should be treated by a multidisciplinary team, including 
a high-risk obstetrician and anesthesiologist during the pre-conception, 
pregnancy, and peripartum period. Management of SM during pregnancy 
involves alleviation of symptoms related to mast cell activation with the 
use of acceptable medications to minimize potential harm to the fetus. 
Breastfeeding by patients with SM should be done in consultation with a 
pediatrician and International Board-Certified Lactation Consultant 
(IBCLC). 

 

 

 

 

 

Avoidance of known triggers and prophylactic anti-mediator drug therapy 
(corticosteroids, antihistamines, and epinephrine) are standard 
approaches during pregnancy and the early postpartum period.223-225 
Cytoreductive therapy with peginterferon alfa-2a is an option for patients 
who are pregnant with severe SM refractory to conventional therapy, 
although there are limited data regarding the use of peginterferon alfa-2a 
in pregnancy. It should be used only if benefits outweigh potential risk to 
the fetus.226 However, the use of cladribine, imatinib, midostaurin, and

nodes.text: General Diagnostic Studies • History and physical (H&P), including prior history of mast cell activation symptoms; history of anaphylaxis; potential triggers; examination for MIS; spleen and liver size by palpation; and documentation of medications, transfusion history, and weight loss • Comprehensive metabolic panel with uric acid, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), and liver function tests (LFTs) • Serum tryptase level • Complete blood count (CBC) with differential • Examination of blood smear (eg, monocytosis, eosinophilia, dysplasia) • Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy with: Flow cytometry: CD34, CD117, CD25, CD30, CD2 IHC: CD117, CD25, CD30, CD2, tryptase Cytogenetics • FISH and/or multigenepanel testing as needed to provide workup for an associated (myeloid) hematologic neoplasm • Molecular testing for KIT D816V using an assay with high sensitivity (eg, allele-specific oligonucleotide quantitative reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction [ASO-qPCR] or digital droplet polymerase chain reaction [ddPCR]).If negative for KIT D816V mutation and eosinophilia is present, then screen for FIP1L1::PDGFRA gene fusion. mast_cell_activation_symptoms_or_anaphyl.definition: The case states the patient has symptoms suggestive of mast cell activation, or has had anaphylaxis.

serum_tryptase_ng_ml.definition: Serum tryptase concentration reported in the case.

serum_tryptase_increased.definition: Clinician judgement that serum tryptase is increased. The flowchart gives no numeric cutoff, so this is not computed from serum_tryptase_ng_ml.

cutaneous_mastocytosis_biopsy_proven_adu.definition: A skin biopsy confirms adult-onset mastocytosis in the skin (MIS).

kit_mutation.definition: Result of KIT mutation testing. d816v_exon17 = KIT D816V (exon 17). exon8_11_mutation = alternate KIT mutation in exons 8-11 found by NGS. other_kit_mutation = any other KIT mutation. wild_type = no KIT mutation found.

kit_d816v_bm_assay_sensitivity_percent.definition: Detection sensitivity (lowest detectable KIT D816V allele fraction, in percent) of the KIT D816V assay performed on bone marrow, as stated in the case. Not stated if the case gives no value.

mlne_excluded_by_fish.definition: The case states that FISH testing for myeloid and/or lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia (MLNE) has excluded MLNE.

mast_cell_morphology_immunophenotype_nor.definition: The case states that mast cell morphology and immunophenotype are normal.

major_sm_criteria_count.definition: Number of major systemic mastocytosis diagnostic criteria fulfilled, as stated in the case.

minor_sm_criteria_count.definition: Number of minor systemic mastocytosis diagnostic criteria fulfilled, as stated in the case. Includes KIT D816V-positive status and CD25-positive mast cells.

b_findings_count.definition: Number of B-findings stated in the case.

c_findings_count.definition: Number of C-findings stated in the case.

organ_damage_meets_trial_criteria.definition: The case states organ damage findings that are eligible under clinical trial response criteria.

symptomatic_sm.definition: The case states whether the systemic mastocytosis is symptomatic (true) or asymptomatic (false).

ahn_present.definition: The case states an associated hematologic neoplasm (AHN) is present.

clinician_states_ahn_prioritized_over_sm.criteria: Does AHN component require prioritization over SM component?
clinician_states_ahn_prioritized_over_sm.definition: Clinician judgement, as stated in the case, that the AHN component requires prioritization over the SM component. The flowchart gives no criteria for this question.

mast_cell_leukemia_type.definition: Type of mast cell leukemia (MCL) stated in the case. none = no MCL.

well_differentiated_sm.definition: Clinician judgement that the systemic mastocytosis is well-differentiated (WDSM).

treatment_response.definition: Response of the current SM or AHN treatment as stated in the case.

disease_progression_to_advanced_sm.definition: The case states that the SM has progressed to an advanced form.

ahn_progression.definition: The case states that the associated hematologic neoplasm (AHN) has progressed.

transformed_to_aml.definition: The case states that the disease has transformed to acute myeloid leukemia (AML).

platelets_x10e9_l.definition: Platelet count reported in the case.

sm_b_finding_class.definition: ISM if 0 or 1 B-findings; SSM if 2 or more B-findings.

asmi_criteria_met.definition: Aggressive systemic mastocytosis (ASMi) criteria: one or more C-findings per WHO/ICC, or eligible organ damage per clinical trial response criteria.

sm_who_criteria_met.definition: WHO systemic mastocytosis diagnostic criteria: at least 1 major plus 1 minor criterion, or 3 or more minor criteria.

sm_icc_criteria_met.definition: ICC systemic mastocytosis diagnostic criteria: 1 or more major criterion, or 3 or more minor criteria.

kit_d816v_negative.definition: KIT D816V-negative by a high-sensitivity bone marrow assay (detection sensitivity 0.01%-0.1%): no D816V result and the KIT mutation result is wild-type or a non-exon-17 mutation.

sm_component_requires_prioritization_ove.definition: SM component requires prioritization over the AHN component. The flowchart example criterion is 1 or more C-findings.

mcl_present.definition: Mast cell leukemia is present (chronic or acute).

advanced_sm.definition: Advanced SM: ASMi criteria met, or SM-AHN with the SM component requiring prioritization, or acute mast cell leukemia.

sm_advancement_status.definition: Advancement category used for the well-differentiated SM branch.

platelets_at_least_50.definition: Platelet count is 50 x10^9/l or higher. False if the platelet count is not stated.

ahn_progression_or_aml_transformation.definition: AHN progression, or transformation to acute myeloid leukemia (AML).
